column2: A man of such kind, goddess, attains the path to heaven, and then, reaching human state, is born in a distinguished family.
There, with vast enjoyments and endowed with all jewels, he is a fitting giver to the worthy and devoted to the practice of dharma.
Esteemed by all beings and saluted by all the world, a man always gains the fruit of his own deeds by himself.
Born in a noble family and lineage always: this dharma I have declared, as the Creator himself said.
But one of fierce conduct, a terror to all beings, who with hands or feet, a rope or a rod,
with clods, posts or devices, afflicts creatures, fair one, bent on harm, crooked-minded, and alarming others,
who attacks creatures and is always a cause of dread, a man of such character and conduct goes to hell.
If by the turning of time he comes to human state, he is born in a low family, tormented with many afflictions.
Hated by the world, the lowest of men, by the fruits of his own deeds, such a one, goddess, is to be recognised among men and kinsmen.
Another looks on all beings with compassion, with a friendly eye, like a father, free of enmity, with senses controlled.
He neither alarms beings nor harms them, with hands and feet well restrained, trusted by all creatures.
With no rope, rod, clods or weapon does he alarm beings, gentle in action and devoted to compassion.
A man of such character and conduct is born in heaven, and there lives joyfully in a divine mansion like a god.
If, when his deeds are exhausted, the mortal is born among men, he is born with little affliction and free of calamity, and prospers happily.
A man who shares in happiness, without toil, always free of dread: this, goddess, is the path of the good, where no affliction is.
These men are seen skilled in reasoning for and against, endowed with knowledge and wisdom, intelligent, knowing meaning; others, god, are dull-witted and devoid of knowledge and wisdom.
By the ripening of what deed does a man become wise? How does a man become of little wit, ill-eyed? Cut this doubt for me, best of those who know all dharma.
Others, god, are blind from birth, others afflicted by disease, and men are seen to be impotent; tell me the cause of that.
[Maheshvara] Those who daily ask brahmins learned in the Veda, the perfected and the knowers of dharma, about good and ill,
avoiding evil deeds and following good ones, gain the path to heaven always and happiness in this world.
If he comes to human state, he is born intelligent, and learning that follows wisdom and fortune arise for him.
Fools who cast an evil eye on other men's wives become, by that evil nature, blind from birth.
Men of evil deeds who with an evil mind look at a naked woman become afflicted with disease here.
Fools of bad conduct who delight in unnatural intercourse with men, very dull-witted, come to impotence.
Men who bind animals, who defile a teacher's bed, and who have indiscriminate intercourse are born impotent.
[Uma] What deed, god, is blameworthy and what blameless, doing which a man obtains the best?
[Maheshvara] One who follows the better path, always asking the twice-born, seeking dharma and desiring merits, attains heaven.
If ever he comes to human state, goddess, he is born intelligent, retentive and wise.
This, goddess, the dharma of the good, which brings prosperity, is to be kept in mind; it was told to you by me for the good of men.
[Uma] Other men, of little knowledge, haters of dharma, do not wish to approach brahmins learned in the Veda.
Some men keep vows, with faith, devoted to self-control; others are without vows, fallen from rules, like rakshasas.
Others are sacrificers and others without oblations; tell me by the ripening of what deed they are so.
[Maheshvara] The bounds of the world's dharmas, made of old, are followed on the authority of tradition, and firm in vows they are seen.
Those who, fallen under delusion, call unrighteousness dharma, and are without vows and have lost the bounds, are called brahmin-demons.
If by effort made in time they are born here as men, they become the lowest of men, without oblation and without vashat.
All this, goddess, has been explained by me to cut your doubt: the ocean of dharma, good and bad among men.
[Maheshvara] You are skilled, calm, self-controlled, without possessiveness, practising dharma. I ask you, fair one; being asked, tell me what I want.
Savitri of Brahma, the virtuous Shachi of Kaushika, Dhumorna of Yama, and Riddhi of Vaishravana,
Gauri of Varuna, Suvarchala of Surya, Rohini of the Moon, the virtuous Svaha of Fire,
and Aditi of Kashyapa: all these have the husband as god; and you, goddess, always ask and attend them.
Therefore I ask you, knower and speaker of dharma, I wish to hear the dharma of women declared by you from the beginning.
[Uma] You are my partner in dharma, of equal character and equal vows, of equal strength and valour, and you have done fierce austerity; what is said by you in particular will be authority.
Women especially are the refuge of the female sex always; a cow goes to a cow, fair-hipped one; such is the standing always in the worlds.
You are half of my body and issued from my half, you do the gods' work and produce the descent of the world.
[Uma] These rivers, god of gods, with the waters of all tirthas, stand near you for the sake of touching you.
Having consulted them, I shall speak in order. One who, having power, does not say "I", is truly called a man.
A woman, lord of beings, always runs after a woman, and these best rivers will be honoured by me.
This is the holy Sarasvati, best of rivers, the first of all rivers, flowing to the sea.
Vipasha, Vitasta, Chandrabhaga, Iravati, Shatadru, Devika, Sindhu, Kaushiki and Gomati,
and this divine river Ganga, surrounded by all tirthas, goddess, who came from the sky to earth, best of all rivers.
Having said this, the wife of the god of gods, best of those who uphold dharma, addressed all those rivers with a smile.
The queen of the gods, a woman fond of dharma, asked those best of rivers, Ganga and the rest, skilled in women's dharma.
This question given by the blessed one concerns women's dharma; having consulted you, I wish to speak on it, auspicious ones.
I see no knowledge in the world that can be accomplished by one alone, nor in heaven; therefore I honour you who go to the sea.
[Bhishma] So all the best rivers, the most holy and auspicious, were asked. Then the divine river Ganga was appointed and honoured her.
Rich in many insights, a woman who knew dharma, pure-smiling, holy, the remover of sin, she addressed the mountain king's daughter, the auspicious goddess.
Endowed with modesty and wisdom, skilled in all knowledge, Ganga, rich in understanding, smiled and spoke.
We are blessed and favoured, goddess, devoted to dharma, since you, honoured by the whole world, honour the rivers, blameless one.
One who, having power, asks and honours a person, surely of undefiled soul, comes to be called wise.
One who asks others, speakers endowed with knowledge and wisdom, skilled in argument, attains a true station.
Otherwise one rich in understanding speaks one thing in an assembly, while a conceited man speaks a weak word differently.
Of divine knowledge, best in heaven, divinely holy, always rising up, you alone, goddess, are fit to instruct us in women's dharma.
[Bhishma] Then the goddess, honoured by Ganga with many virtues, the beautiful woman of the gods, told all of women's dharma in full.
As women's dharma appears to me, rightly, I shall tell it, so that it may be renowned.
This women's dharma was first performed by relatives at the marriage: she becomes her husband's partner in dharma before the fire.
Of good nature, good speech, good conduct and pleasant to see, with undivided mind and fair face, she is her husband's companion in dharma.
She is supreme in dharma and shares in dharma, a woman of virtue who, child, regards her husband as a god.
She who gives service and attendance as to a god, with no other thought, undismayed, of good vows and pleasant to see,
who looks at her husband's face again and again as at a son's face, the virtuous woman of restrained conduct, is the one who practises dharma.
Having heard the auspicious dharma of a couple, made as partners in dharma, with undivided mind and fair face, she is her husband's companion in dharma.
The woman who, even when spoken to harshly or looked at with a cruel eye, keeps a serene face toward her husband, is devoted to her husband.
The fair-hipped one who looks at neither moon, sun nor tree with a male name, apart from her husband, is the one who practises dharma.
The woman who tends a husband poor, sick, wretched or worn by travel as she would a son shares in dharma.
The woman who is restrained and skilled, who is a mother of sons, dear to her husband, her husband her life, shares in dharma.
She who always gives service and attendance undismayed, cheerful and modest, shares in dharma.
A woman who has no longing for pleasures, enjoyments, lordship or happiness apart from her husband shares in dharma.
Always rising at dawn, devoted to serving elders, with the house well swept, and plastered with cow dung,
always devoted to the fire rite, ever giving flowers and offerings, setting aside portions for gods, guests and servants with her husband,
eating what remains, rightly and by rule, keeping her people content and nourished, a woman is joined with dharma.
She who pleases the feet of her mother-in-law and father-in-law, virtuous, always devoted to mother and father, is rich in austerity.
The woman who supports with food brahmins, the weak, the helpless, the wretched, the blind and the needy shares in the devoted wife's vow.
She who always keeps the hard-to-keep vow with a light heart, her mind on her husband and her good, shares in the devoted wife's vow.
This is merit and austerity, and this is eternal heaven: the woman whose supreme is her husband, devoted to her husband, is auspicious.
For a husband is a woman's god, a husband her kin, a husband her refuge; there is no refuge equal to a husband, nor deity like a husband.
Whether or not heaven is equal to a husband's favour for a woman, I would not wish for heaven if you, Maheshvara, were displeased.
If a husband, poor or sick, were somehow to command what should not be done, or unrighteousness, or even the destruction of life,
or if he were in distress, among enemies, or afflicted by a brahmin's curse, considering the dharmas of distress, it should be done without hesitation.
This, god, is the women's dharma as I have told it at your word; the woman who is so shares in dharma.
[Bhishma] Thus addressed, the lord of the gods honoured the mountain's daughter and dismissed the worlds with all his attendants.
Then the hosts of spirits and the rivers went as they had come, and the gandharvas and apsarases, bowing their heads to Bhava.
[Yudhishthira] Who is the one deity in the world, and what the one refuge? Praising whom, worshipping whom, do men gain the good?
What dharma do you hold highest of all dharmas? Reciting what is a creature freed from the bond of birth and rebirth?
[Bhishma] A man who always rises early and praises, with the thousand names, the lord of the world, god of gods, the endless Supreme Person,
and constantly worships that very imperishable Person with devotion, meditating on him, praising and bowing to him, and sacrificing to him,
praising always Vishnu, without beginning or end, great lord of all worlds, overseer of the worlds, would pass beyond all sorrows.
Devoted to brahmins, knower of all dharma, increaser of the worlds' fame, lord of the world, great being, origin and source of all beings,
this I hold the highest dharma of all dharmas: that a man should always worship the lotus-eyed one with devotion by hymns.
He who is the supreme great radiance, the supreme great austerity, the supreme great Brahman, the supreme refuge,
from whom all beings arise at the beginning of the age, and into whom they go to dissolution again at the end of the age,
of that chief of the worlds, lord of the universe, O king, hear from me the thousand names of Vishnu, which remove fear of sin.
